Article Title: Jennifer Lopez became Grameen America’s ambassador in 2022; the nonprofit now reports $8 billion in cumulative loans and 291,602 small businesses served as it expands access to business capital
Article Text:
Grameen America combines affordable loans, financial education, savings support and community networks to empower underserved women entrepreneurs.

A partnership for Latina businesswomen

Access to building companies

Expanding national presence

Invest in economic mobility

For women starting businesses on a shoestring budget, access to capital can mean the difference between an idea staying a dream or becoming a living. Grameen America's model has been centered on bridging this gap, particularly for women who live in communities that require more assistance. The partnership with Jennifer Lopez brought a star-studded voice to that mission, driving more awareness around financial inclusion and Latina entrepreneurship.Lopez became Grameen America's National Ambassador in 2022 as part of her philanthropy, the blog reports. The partnership was created to assist Latina business owners who have historically been left out of mainstream financial services. Grameen America provides business capital, financial education, credit and asset building, and peer networks to women living below the federal poverty line. As an ambassador, Lopez would mentor Latina entrepreneurs, promote financial literacy and encourage pathways toward greater financial independence. The collaboration also aided Grameen America’s larger mission of reaching more Latina entrepreneurs throughout the United States.The organisation’s approach is more than just lending. Members receive ongoing financial literacy training and have their loan payments reported to credit bureaus. This enables members to establish their financial identities and gain access to improved financial services in the future. The Grameen America Blog has written about the extent of the problem for women entrepreneurs . Latino-owned businesses have grown quickly, but access to traditional lending has been uneven.Women also receive a tiny fraction of small business loans from mainstream financial institutions.Grameen America’s model seeks to address these gaps by providing a combination of affordable capital, education, savings and community-based support.The organization has grown tremendously since then. Grameen America has provided more than $5 billion in affordable capital to more than 230,000 entrepreneurs in 29 U.S. cities, according to its website. “Reported figures to date indicate cumulative lending of around $8 billion, reaching 291,602 small businesses. And its aspirations for long-term growth are even bigger. The organization’s mission is to reach 750,000 entrepreneurs over the next 10 years and deploy $40 billion in loan capital to underserved communities.According to Grameen America’s website, the nonprofit will launch a five-year campaign supported by $600 million in new fundraising that combines philanthropy and debt capital. The initiative, combined with internally generated funding, is expected to help fund an estimated $1 billion investment to expand its program.The end goal is to help entrepreneurs move from financial stability to long-term economic mobility. Grameen America is dedicated to empowering neighborhood economies by assisting families in building generational wealth and financial independence through small business ownership.The mission was given a celebrity profile by Lopez, but the organization’s growing lending network suggests a larger ambition: to offer women historically excluded from the mainstream financial world the chance to own a business and access financial opportunity.Images Courtesy: istock and Instagram/jlo
Article Summary: Lopez became Grameen America's National Ambassador in 2022 as part of her philanthropy. The partnership was created to assist Latina business owners who have historically been left out of mainstream financial services. The organization has provided more than $5 billion in affordable capital to more than 230,000 entrepreneurs in 29 U.S. cities.

Article Title: A mother says her Doberman kept crying and refusing to leave her six-month-old son; doctors later found the baby's heart was racing at 280 beats per minute and diagnosed a rare electrical condition
Article Text:
Doberman's behaviour has raised concerns about Alexander's health twice. (Photo: Youtube/SWNS)

Baby's heartbeat remains high

What causes Wolff-Parkinson-White syndrome?

Dog's behaviour raises concern again

Poll Vote & Share your view How concerned would you be if a pet exhibited unusual behavior around your child? Very concerned Somewhat concerned Not concerned at all 3k+ users shared opinion today 5k+ users already voted today 3k+ users shared opinion today Share Opinion

A pet Doberman's unusual behaviour around a six-month-old baby in England led his mother to seek medical help, after which doctors discovered that the child had a dangerously fast heartbeat of 280 beats per minute. The incident happened in September when Kim Reynolds, 41, from Shepton Mallet in Somerset, noticed that her dog, Saraya, was repeatedly crying and refusing to leave her son Alexander alone, SWNS reported. Doctors later diagnosed the baby with Wolff-Parkinson-White syndrome, a condition that affects the electrical signals controlling the heartbeat.Kim, a first-time mother and former canine hydrotherapist, was familiar with dogs but had never seen Saraya behave this way around Alexander. The Doberman appeared unusually concerned about the baby and became upset whenever he was moved away from her. At first, Kim could not understand what was troubling the animal.Later that day, Alexander began showing signs of illness, so she took him to the emergency department at Royal Bournemouth Hospital.By the time they reached the hospital, Alexander had stopped crying. Kim wondered whether the visit had been necessary.However, when doctors examined him, they found that his heart was beating at 280 beats per minute and the baby needed immediate treatment to bring his heart rhythm under control.Doctors first attempted to slow Alexander's heartbeat using cold water and ice. Kim recalled that medical staff placed her son in a container of icy water as part of the procedure. She found the experience distressing, particularly when she heard him scream.The treatment was attempted twice, but Alexander's heartbeat remained unusually fast. According to Kim's account, his head was submerged for around 10 seconds during the procedure. When the attempts failed, he was returned to her lap.Kim then asked whether doctors could use medication instead. Alexander was given medicine intravenously, and his heart rate eventually came down after three doses.Once his condition had been stabilised, he was taken by ambulance to Poole Hospital for further care. Kim remained in hospital with her son for two nights while doctors investigated what had caused his heartbeat to become so fast.Two days after the first emergency visit, Alexander was diagnosed with Wolff-Parkinson-White syndrome.According to MedBound Times, Wolff-Parkinson-White syndrome, also called WPW syndrome, is a congenital heart condition that involves an extra electrical connection between the heart's upper and lower chambers.Normally, electrical signals travel through the heart along a controlled pathway, helping maintain a regular heartbeat. In people with WPW syndrome, the additional connection can allow signals to travel differently, sometimes triggering episodes in which the heart beats much faster than normal.These episodes can involve supraventricular tachycardia (SVT), a condition in which the heartbeat becomes abnormally fast. In young children, warning signs can include breathing difficulties, pale skin, irritability and restlessness.Doctors commonly use an electrocardiogram, or ECG, to identify WPW syndrome. The test records the heart's electrical activity. Other investigations, including heart monitoring and an echocardiogram, may also be recommended depending on the patient's symptoms.Alexander now receives propranolol, a beta-blocker used to help control his heart rate. Kim gives him the medicine three times daily through a syringe. She says he has become comfortable taking it and does not resist the treatment.The September hospital visit was not the only occasion when Saraya's actions made Kim worry about Alexander's health.Later that month, the baby was sitting in his bouncer when the Doberman began behaving unusually again. Saraya stayed close to him, licked his hands and repeatedly looked towards Kim.Remembering what had happened earlier, Kim immediately wondered whether Alexander was experiencing another episode of SVT. She checked his pulse but also noticed that his throat looked red.Kim decided to take him to hospital again. This time, doctors found that he had bacterial tonsillitis rather than another reported episode of his heart condition. Alexander was prescribed penicillin.Saraya has not received specialist training to identify medical conditions and is not registered as an assistance dog. Nevertheless, Kim says the two incidents have made her pay close attention whenever the Doberman behaves differently around her son.
Article Summary: Kim Reynolds, 41, from Somerset, noticed that her dog, Saraya, was repeatedly crying and refusing to leave her son Alexander alone. Doctors later diagnosed the baby with Wolff-Parkinson-White syndrome, a condition that affects the electrical signals controlling the heartbeat. Two days after the first emergency visit, doctors found that Alexander had bacterial tonsillitis.

Article Title: US midterms 2026: Early voting surpasses 50.5 million, Texas sees significant voter turnout increase
Article Text:
Over 50.5 million early votes cast by Saturday morning/Image: Reuters

More than 50.5 million Americans have voted early ahead of the 2026 US midterm elections, nearly five million more than the total recorded during the 2022 midterms. The increase comes as both parties face closely contested races that could determine control of Congress for the final two years of President Donald Trump's second term.Data from the University of Florida's Election Lab showed that early voting had surpassed 50.5 million by Saturday morning, ahead of Tuesday's election.Among states that track voters' party affiliations, registered Democrats accounted for 10.7 million early ballots, compared with 7.8 million from registered Republicans. These figures reflect the political registration of voters who have cast ballots and do not indicate which candidates they have supported.The higher number of Democratic voters comes as Republicans face competitive contests in states that have traditionally favoured the party. Dissatisfaction with Trump's presidency and concerns about the cost of living have also become prominent issues in the campaign.Republicans currently hold a 53-47 majority in the Senate and are seeking to retain control of the chamber. Democrats are targeting traditionally Republican-leaning states, including Texas, Alaska and Kansas, where competitive races could help them secure a majority.Texas has become a major focus of the contest, with more than seven million people having already voted early, as per the University data. This is around 1.5 million more than the number recorded in the state during the 2022 midterms.The increase is also evident in Harris County, which includes Houston. By Wednesday, 862,700 people had cast early ballots there, compared with 564,500 at the same point in the 2022 election, the Associated Press analysis has found.Harris County has consistently backed Democratic candidates in recent elections. In 2024, Kamala Harris defeated Trump in the county by nearly six percentage points in the presidential election. Democratic Senate candidate Colin Allred also won the county by roughly 11 percentage points over Republican incumbent Ted Cruz.This year's Texas Senate contest has drawn national attention, with Republican Attorney General Ken Paxton facing Democratic candidate James Talarico. Republican Governor Greg Abbott is also seeking re-election against Democrat Gina Hinojosa.Early voting has also increased in other states with competitive Senate races. South Carolina, which Trump won by nearly 18 percentage points in the 2024 presidential election, has recorded an 83% rise in early voting compared with the 2022 midterms, as per AP analysis.In Kansas, where Republicans face another closely contested Senate race, early voting is up 34%. Maine has recorded a 44% increase, while Michigan has seen a rise of 32%, the AP reported.The midterm elections will determine the composition of the House of Representatives and Senate for the remaining two years of Trump's term. Rising prices of food, petrol and other essentials, the war involving Iran and concerns about government corruption have featured in the political debate ahead of the vote.Trump has held rallies across several states to support Republican candidates, including in areas that have traditionally been considered safe for the party. During his campaign appearances, he has repeatedly commented on candidates' physical appearance and dismissed concerns about rising petrol prices, pointing instead to the profits of fossil fuel companies.Speaking at a rally in Florida on Friday night, Trump acknowledged the demands of his campaign schedule.“I thought this was it,” he said. “I thought I could relax. Twenty-eight days of this crap in a row is a lot. It’s a lot.”
Article Summary: More than 50.5 million Americans have voted early ahead of the 2026 US midterm elections. This is nearly five million more than the total recorded during the 2022 midterms. Both parties face closely contested races that could determine control of Congress for the final two years of President Donald Trump's second term.

Article Title: Violent protests rock Bangladesh garment hubs as workers demand a steep pay hike
Article Text:
Police used tear gas and sound grenades to disperse crowds as demonstrations intensified. (Reuters)

What's the demand

Wage board formed, but protests continue

Violent protests have erupted in Bangladesh's garment industry as workers demand a sharp increase in their minimum monthly wage from 12,500 taka to 30,000 taka. Clashes, vandalism and road blockades have been reported in Dhaka and Gazipur, prompting authorities to deploy police and Border Guard Bangladesh personnel to restore order.The unrest, which began on Saturday, escalated on Sunday in industrial areas such as Mirpur in Dhaka and Konabari in Gazipur. Protesters allegedly vandalised factories, attacked police outposts with stones and set police vehicles on fire. Several major roads were blocked using barricades, disrupting movement.Police used tear gas and sound grenades to disperse crowds as demonstrations intensified. Border Guard Bangladesh units were also deployed alongside police to maintain security in the affected areas.Garment workers are demanding a monthly minimum wage of 30,000 taka, more than twice the existing minimum of 12,500 taka. Their demand comes amid a recent government announcement of a new pay scale for public sector employees, which is expected to nearly double their salaries and benefits.Workers are seeking a comparable improvement in their earnings, arguing for a substantial increase in wages. However, factory owners say they are struggling with declining orders, stagnant product prices and rising costs of imported raw materials.They have argued that meeting the workers' demand would be difficult under current conditions.The Bangladesh government has formed a wage board to decide on a revised minimum wage for garment workers. However, the move has not brought the demonstrations to an end, with workers continuing to protest for higher pay.The dispute has put the spotlight on Bangladesh's ready-made garment (RMG) industry, which grew rapidly from the late 1970s and early 1980s to become the backbone of the country's export economy.The sector accounts for more than 80 per cent of Bangladesh's export earnings and employs around four million people. Women make up an estimated 60 to 70 per cent of its workforce, making the industry a major source of employment and economic opportunity for them.
Article Summary: Clashes, vandalism and road blockades have been reported in Dhaka and Gazipur. Protesters allegedly vandalised factories, attacked police outposts with stones and set police vehicles on fire. Police used tear gas and sound grenades to disperse crowds as demonstrations intensified.

Not every home in Los Angeles has a famous name. But this one does. The sprawling estate at 77 Beverly Park Lane, where Prince once lived, is on the market for $54.5 million after a $13.5 million price cut, Mansion Global reported. The megamansion was initially listed for $68 million, according to The Real Deal.The house sits at 77 Beverly Park Lane on two flat acres inside a guard-gated community. The late singer, né Prince Rogers Nelson, reportedly lived in the property and recorded there between 2008 and 2009, according to the outlet. The property was owned by an entity linked to Vanna White’s ex-husband, developer George Santopietro. He built the mansion in 2010. However, the mansion was built in 2007, according to its listing on Zillow. Branden Williams and Rayni Williams of The Beverly Hills Estates have listed the property.The megamansion sits on what the listing describes as “the most prolific property in Beverly Park”. It adds: “A dramatic arrival unfolds into interiors defined by soaring ceilings, refined architectural detail, expansive volumes, and millions spent on stones and finishes sourced from around the world.Walls of glass frame the surrounding landscape, filling the home with natural light and seamlessly connecting indoor living with the estate's outdoor spaces. ”The mansion spans 27,000 sq ft and has nine bedrooms and 15 bathrooms. The house is built for grand-scale entertaining, with a multimillion-dollar private theatre and an extraordinary wine cellar. It also comes with a gym and parking for more than 50 cars. The grounds are just as striking. The landscaping was designed by the renowned landscape designer behind San Ysidro Ranch. “Resort-calibre grounds showcase manicured lawns, lush rose and vegetable gardens, and entertaining terraces with multiple fire pits, an outdoor kitchen, pizza oven, grills, and dining areas, creating a private oasis,” the listing says.Beverly Park has long attracted people who value wealth and privacy. Sylvester Stallone lived there, and Adele bought his former estate in 2020 for $58 million. Mark Wahlberg also owned a home in the enclave. Paris Hilton and her husband, Carter Reum, bought that property last year.The megamansion first hit the market in April for $68 million. That was a high figure even for this neighbourhood. Other sellers on the same street have learnt the same lesson. In 2022, Villa Firenze came down by about $41 million from an asking price of $120 million, while Wahlberg cut his own asking price from $87.5 million to $79.5 million that same year.Those cuts suggest buyers in this enclave are willing to pay top dollar, but only for a home that matches recent sales. However, the Prince connection adds historical significance to the listing. The recent discount might also attract more interest from potential buyers.
Article Summary: The sprawling estate at 77 Beverly Park Lane, where Prince once lived, is on the market for $54.5 million. The mansion spans 27,000 sq ft and has nine bedrooms and 15 bathrooms. The house is built for grand-scale entertaining, with a multimillion-dollar private theatre and an extraordinary wine cellar.
